audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Kings / Melakhim Aleph chapter 8, first-pass draft aligned to public-domain verse structure; formal liturgical and witness audit remains required.
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for ark procession, mass animal sacrifice, cloud and glory, temple containment tension, covenant and dynasty, judicial oaths, defeat and land return, drought, famine and illness theology, foreigner prayer, war prayer, captivity, forgiveness, animal slaughter, and national feast.

verses.restored: Then Solomon assembled elders of Israel, all heads of tribes, and leaders of ancestral houses of children of Israel to King Solomon in Jerusalem, to bring ark of covenant of YHWH up from City of David, which is Zion.
All men of Israel assembled to King Solomon at feast in month Ethanim, seventh month.
All elders of Israel came, and priests carried ark.
They brought up ark of YHWH, tent of meeting, and all holy vessels in tent; priests and Levites brought them up.
King Solomon and all congregation of Israel assembled to him were before ark, sacrificing sheep and cattle that could not be counted for multitude.
Priests brought ark of covenant of YHWH to its place, inner sanctuary of house, most holy place, beneath wings of cherubim.
Cherubim spread both wings over place of ark and covered ark and its poles from above.
Poles were extended so their ends were seen from holy place before inner sanctuary but not seen outside; they are there until this day.
Nothing was in ark except two stone tablets Moses placed there at Horeb, where YHWH cut covenant with children of Israel when they came from land of Egypt.
When priests came out from holy place, cloud filled house of YHWH.
Priests could not stand to minister because of cloud, for glory of YHWH filled house of YHWH.
Then Solomon said, YHWH said YHWH would dwell in thick darkness.
Building, I have built a house of dwelling for you, an established place for you to dwell forever.
The king turned his face and blessed all congregation of Israel, while all congregation stood.
He said, Blessed be YHWH, Divine of Israel, who spoke with mouth to David my father and fulfilled with hand, saying:
From day I brought my people Israel out of Egypt, I chose no city from all tribes of Israel to build house for my name there; but I chose David to be over my people Israel.
It was in heart of David my father to build house for name of YHWH, Divine of Israel.
YHWH said to David my father, Because it was in your heart to build house for my name, you did well that it was in your heart.
Nevertheless you shall not build house; your son coming from your body shall build house for my name.
YHWH established word spoken. I arose in place of David my father, sat upon throne of Israel as YHWH spoke, and built house for name of YHWH, Divine of Israel.
There I set a place for ark containing covenant of YHWH, which YHWH cut with our ancestors when bringing them out from land of Egypt.
Solomon stood before altar of YHWH in presence of all congregation of Israel and spread his hands toward heavens.
He said, YHWH, Divine of Israel, there is no Divine like you in heavens above or earth beneath, keeping covenant and covenant-kindness with servants walking before you with all heart.
You kept for your servant David my father what you spoke; you spoke with mouth and fulfilled with hand this day.

Now YHWH, Divine of Israel, keep for your servant David my father what you spoke: A man shall not be cut off for you before me from sitting upon throne of Israel, if your children guard their way to walk before me as you walked.
Now, Divine of Israel, please let your word be confirmed, which you spoke to your servant David my father.
But will Divine truly dwell upon earth? Look, heavens and heavens of heavens cannot contain you—how much less this house I built.
Yet turn toward prayer of your servant and his plea, YHWH my Divine, to hear cry and prayer your servant prays before you this day.
Let your eyes be open toward this house night and day, toward place of which you said, My name shall be there, to hear prayer your servant prays toward this place.
Hear plea of your servant and your people Israel when they pray toward this place; hear in heavens, your dwelling place; hear and forgive.
If a person sins against neighbor and an oath is placed upon him to make him swear, and oath comes before your altar in this house,
hear in heavens, act, and judge your servants: condemn guilty by bringing his way upon his head, and justify righteous by giving according to righteousness.
When your people Israel are struck before enemy because they sinned against you, and they return, confess your name, pray, and plead to you in this house,
hear in heavens, forgive sin of your people Israel, and return them to land you gave their ancestors.
When heavens are shut and there is no rain because they sinned against you, if they pray toward this place, confess your name, and turn from sin when you afflict them,
hear in heavens, forgive sin of your servants and your people Israel, teach them good way they should walk, and give rain upon your land which you gave your people as inheritance.
If there is famine in land, pestilence, blight, mildew, locust, devouring insect, or enemy besieges them in land of their gates—any plague, any sickness—
every prayer, every plea made by any human or all your people Israel, each knowing plague of own heart and spreading hands toward this house,
hear in heavens your dwelling place, forgive, act, and give to each according to ways, whose heart you know—for you alone know heart of all children of humanity—
so they may revere you all days they live upon land you gave our ancestors.
Also concerning foreigner who is not of your people Israel but comes from distant land for your name's sake—
for they shall hear of your great name, strong hand, and outstretched arm—when the foreigner comes and prays toward this house,

hear in heavens your dwelling place and do according to all foreigner calls to you for, so all peoples of earth may know your name, revere you as your people Israel, and know this house I built is called by your name.
If your people go out to battle against enemy by way you send them and pray to YHWH toward city you chose and house I built for your name,
hear in heavens their prayer and plea and uphold their cause.
If they sin against you—for there is no human who does not sin—and you become angry, give them before enemy, and captors carry them captive to enemy land, far or near,
if they return to heart in land where carried captive, turn, and plead to you in land of captors, saying, We sinned, acted perversely, and did wickedness,
and return to you with all heart and soul in land of enemies who carried them captive, and pray toward their land you gave ancestors, city you chose, and house I built for your name,
hear their prayer and plea in heavens your dwelling place and uphold their cause.
Forgive your people who sinned against you and all transgressions they transgressed against you; give them compassion before captors, so captors have compassion upon them.
For they are your people and inheritance, whom you brought from Egypt, from midst of iron furnace.
Let your eyes be open to plea of your servant and plea of your people Israel, hearing them in all they call to you.
For you separated them for yourself as inheritance from all peoples of earth, as you spoke by hand of Moses your servant when you brought our ancestors from Egypt, Lord YHWH.
When Solomon finished praying all this prayer and plea to YHWH, he arose from before altar of YHWH, from kneeling upon knees with hands spread to heavens.
He stood and blessed all congregation of Israel with loud voice, saying:
Blessed be YHWH, who gave rest to people Israel according to all spoken. Not one word failed from all good word spoken by hand of Moses servant.
May YHWH our Divine be with us as with our ancestors; may YHWH not leave or abandon us.
May YHWH incline our hearts toward YHWH, to walk in all ways and keep commands, statutes, and judgments commanded to our ancestors.
May these words with which I pleaded before YHWH be near YHWH our Divine day and night, to uphold cause of servant and cause of people Israel, each day's matter in its day,
so all peoples of earth may know YHWH is Divine; there is no other.
Let your heart be whole with YHWH our Divine, to walk in statutes and keep commands as this day.
The king and all Israel with him sacrificed sacrifice before YHWH.
Solomon sacrificed peace offerings to YHWH: twenty-two thousand cattle and one hundred twenty thousand sheep. Thus king and all children of Israel dedicated house of YHWH.

That day king consecrated middle of court before house of YHWH, for there he offered burnt offering, grain offering, and fat of peace offerings, because bronze altar before YHWH was too small to contain them.
At that time Solomon held feast, and all Israel with him, a great assembly from entrance of Hamath to wadi of Egypt, before YHWH our Divine, seven days and seven days—fourteen days.
On eighth day he sent people away. They blessed king and went to tents joyful and glad of heart for all goodness YHWH had done for David servant and Israel people.

translation_notes: Solomon explicitly admits that heavens cannot contain the Divine. The temple bears the name and directs prayer; it does not imprison, monopolize, or geographically exhaust Divine presence.
The ark contains covenant tablets tied to liberation from Egypt. Sacred memory should resist new systems of forced labor and domination.
Cloud and glory interrupt priestly service. Religious professionals do not control Divine manifestation.

The prayer repeatedly interprets defeat, drought, famine, epidemic, illness, and captivity through sin. These ancient theological claims must never be used to blame modern victims, disabled people, sick people, disaster survivors, or occupied populations.
Judicial oath language assumes Divine exposure of guilt but does not replace evidence, due process, protection from false accusation, or appeal.
The foreigner's prayer is welcomed and heard without ethnic conversion being stated. Sacred access extends beyond Israel.
Prayer for battle cannot authorize aggressive war, nationalism, conquest, atrocities, or certainty that one's military cause is Divine.
Captivity prayer centers repentance but also asks captors to show compassion. It must not justify enslavement, deportation, or collective exile.
The dedication sacrifices an enormous number of animals. Festival joy cannot erase animal death, labor, waste, environmental load, or unequal access to abundance.
The congregation blesses the king, but covenant faithfulness remains the standard by which the king is judged.
safety_note: Do not weaponize this prayer to blame sickness, famine, drought, military defeat, displacement, or captivity on victims' sins. Do not use the temple to exclude foreigners or sanctify war. Center forgiveness, compassion, accessible prayer, justice, and the Divine who cannot be contained.
